q: What does it do on GitHub?
a: It writes files only. Branch protection, merge settings, labels and secrets are yours to change, so it lists the commands instead of running them. On a private repository, CodeQL needs the paid GitHub Code Security, so init asks before it adds that workflow.

npx skills update updates the skill. upgrade then compares what it generated, hash by hash, with the new templates, and writes only the files you have not edited. New answers given with --config are saved, so the next run starts from them.

q: What stops an agent working on main?
a: The generated rules tell it to check the branch before its first edit and to branch without asking. Git then refuses a commit on main and a push to it. Branch protection on GitHub, which you enable, is the final rule.

q: Does spec-driven work for every stack?
a: Not yet. The spec reviewer assumes a src/ layout and reads TypeScript test titles, so it suits TypeScript projects and is refused for a monorepo. Everything else works for every stack.
